The Definitive Uganda
Mountain Gorilla Trekking Guide

Everything you need to know about tracking endangered mountain gorillas across Bwindi Impenetrable National Park and Mgahinga Gorilla National Park: permits, sectors, habituation experiences, and preparation.

Compare Tracking vs Habituation Reserve 2026 / 2027 Permits
Permit Options

Standard Tracking vs Habituation Experience

Uganda is the only country on Earth where visitors can participate in official wild gorilla habituation alongside research biologists.

Option One

Standard Gorilla Tracking

UWA Tariff $800 per foreign non-resident

Hike into the mountain rainforest in a group of up to eight visitors accompanied by an armed UWA lead ranger and two trackers with machetes. Once the habituated family is located, you spend exactly one hour observing them feeding, grooming, and playing.

Observation Time: Exactly 1 hour with the family
Group Size: Maximum 8 guests per gorilla family
Available Sectors: Buhoma, Ruhija, Rushaga, Nkuringo, Mgahinga
Habituation Level: Fully habituated wild groups accustomed to humans
Inquire for Standard Tracking
Exclusive to Uganda
Option Two

Gorilla Habituation Experience

UWA Tariff $1,500 per foreign non-resident

Spend four uninterrupted hours with a semi-habituated gorilla family in the presence of senior primatologists, behavioral researchers, and trackers. Learn how researchers accustom wild primates to human presence without altering their natural social hierarchy.

Observation Time: 4 full hours in their immediate presence
Group Size: Capped strictly at 4 guests per group
Available Sectors: Exclusively in Rushaga (Southern Bwindi)
Science Immersion: Direct interaction with senior primate research teams
Inquire for Habituation Experience
Geography & Trailheads

The Four Wilderness Sectors of Bwindi

Bwindi is divided into four distinct administrative sectors. Your gorilla permit specifies the exact sector, dictating your lodge location and road logistics.

Northern Bwindi

Buhoma Sector

The historic birthplace of gorilla tourism in Uganda (established 1993). Lower elevation (around 1,400m), gentler initial hiking slopes, and home to some of Uganda's most legendary luxury lodges.

Key Lodge Partners: Sanctuary Gorilla Forest Camp, Bwindi Lodge by Volcanoes, Mahogany Springs.
Eastern Bwindi

Ruhija Sector

Highest elevation sector (up to 2,350m) characterized by dramatic misty valleys and cold alpine mornings. Renowned among ornithologists as Africa's premier Albertine Rift birding site.

Key Lodge Partners: Bakiga Lodge, Ruhija Gorilla Safari Lodge, Kiho Gorilla Safari Lodge.
Southern Bwindi

Rushaga Sector

Holds the highest concentration of habituated gorilla families in Uganda, as well as the exclusive 4-hour Gorilla Habituation program. Steep, rewarding terrain with deep ancient ravines.

Key Lodge Partners: Four Gorillas Lodge, Chameleon Hill Lodge, Rushaga Gorilla Camp.
South-Western Bwindi

Nkuringo Sector

Perched on a high ridge with staggering 360-degree vistas across the Kashasha river valley and the eight Virunga volcanoes. The most physically demanding yet scenic trailhead.

Key Lodge Partners: Clouds Mountain Gorilla Lodge, Nkuringo Bwindi Gorilla Lodge.
Field Preparation

Fitness, Terrain & Altitude Advisory

Trekking takes place between 1,160 and 2,607 meters above sea level. There are no paved trails: rangers clear paths with machetes through thick undergrowth, tangled vines, and steep muddy inclines. Treks can range from 1.5 hours to over 6 hours depending on where the gorilla family nested the previous night.

Hire a Local Porter ($20 per trek)

We strongly advise every guest to hire a local community porter at the park briefing station. Beyond carrying your daypack and camera gear, porters offer a steady hand over slippery river crossings. This is also one of the most direct ways tourism revenue reaches frontier farming families.

The 'African Helicopter' Sedan Chair

For elderly or mobility-impaired guests who dream of seeing mountain gorillas, the Uganda Wildlife Authority arranges comfortable steel-framed stretcher chairs carried by a team of 12 coordinated local porters ($350 to $500 fee). Nobody is left behind.

Checklist

Essential Gorilla Trekking Gear

  • 1 Broken-In Waterproof Hiking Boots: Essential for gripping steep muddy clay ridges and slippery tree roots.
  • 2 Gardening or Sturdy Gloves: Protects your hands from stinging nettles, prickly thorns, and rough branches when pulling yourself up slopes.
  • 3 Long Moisture-Wicking Pants & Gaiters: Tucking your trousers into long socks or gaiters prevents safari ants from crawling up your legs.
  • 4 Lightweight Breathable Rain Jacket: Bwindi is a tropical rainforest; downpours occur suddenly regardless of season.
  • 5 Medical Face Masks: Mandatory during the actual observation window to protect gorillas from human respiratory viruses.
  • 6 Waterproof Camera Dry Bag: Protect your lens and sensor from moisture and sudden rainforest mist.
Primate Health Protocol

Conservation Etiquette in the Field

Mountain gorillas share over 98% of our DNA and possess zero antibodies against common human pathogens. Our field code strictly protects their fragile population.

10-Meter Distance Rule

Maintain at least 10 meters distance from gorillas at all times. If a curious youngster approaches you, stand completely calm, avoid direct eye contact, and let your ranger direct the encounter.

Zero Flash Photography

Flash photography is strictly forbidden as it can provoke aggressive defense charges from dominant silverbacks. Check your camera shutter and disable autofocus assist lamps prior to the briefing.

Illness Self-Reporting

Anyone exhibiting active cold, flu, cough, or diarrhea symptoms will not be permitted to track gorillas. A 50% refund or permit rescheduling is supported by UWA medical protocols.
